#### Description

When installing an image from ONIE, it failed to get an IP address for eth0, which result in no way to access the DUT except console.  This issue can be reproduced from the master image with the latest commit hash c89567750.  As I tested, if I revert https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/commit/c8b5daed27fa29a1d993379d68dbbe5b05dcfc0d, this issue disappeared, so I believe this commit cause the issue.

This issue can be reproduced easily on different setups by simply install the image from ONIE,  and when it boots up, access through the console, manually issue command "dhclient eth0 -v" can have the IP address assigned correctly.

comments.author: keboliu
comments.body: I was able to identify the problematic commit hash, it's  https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/commit/c8b5daed27fa29a1d993379d68dbbe5b05dcfc0d,  after I reverted it, I see the eth0 can obtain IP address as before.

comments.author: saiarcot895
comments.body:
I see the cause of this issue: ifupdown2 3.0.0 added a check after starting dhclient to see if a new IP address was added (if dhclient succeeded in getting a new address); this check wasn't there in 1.2.8. This alone would be fine (and in fact match the behavior of ifupdown), but we're installing a policy file at `/etc/network/ifupdown2/policy.d/ifupdown2_policy.json` with `"dhcp-wait" : "no"` (packaged from `files/dhcp/ifupdown2_policy.json`).

What this does is it tells ifupdown2 to start dhclient with the `-nw` flag, which tells dhclient to become a daemon immediately, before it gets an IP address. This lets ifupdown2 continue ahead without waiting for dhclient to get an IP address and then become a daemon. This behavior is the same in 1.2.8 and 3.0.0. What's new in 3.0.0 is that because it's checking for a new IP address after dhclient becomes a daemon, since dhclient takes a second or two to actually get and install the IP address, ifupdown2 will see that there's no new IP addresses, and so kill the dhclient process and release any leases that got acquired.

I think the only fix here might be to remove `"dhcp-wait" : "no"` from that policy file, but I'm not sure why it was added there in the first place.

comments.author: rajendra-dendukuri
comments.body: This option was added to allow multiple dhclient instances to start in parallel. When dhclient is run on in-band interfaces(typically 32-48ports), having the no wait option ensures that "systemctl restart networking" is not blocked for a lot of time. Yes, if we remove it, there can be issues when using ZTP. Also, if the OOB interface is not receiving DHCP offer as soon as the switch boots, it may result in slower start of services if they are blocked on eth0 getting an ip address. If there is a behavior change in ifupdown2 3.0.0 compared to v1.2.8, I would flag that to the ifupdown2 maintainer. The fix ideally should be to have a new policy setting which allows things to run like it was in v1.2.8.

comments.author: lguohan
comments.body: can this ifupdown2 policy be per interface? the issue is on eth0 now.

comments.author: saiarcot895
comments.body: For this particular policy entry, it looks like ifupdown2 checks only the global policy setting, not the per-interface policy setting. They do have the ability to specify per-interface policy settings, but this one is calling a method that only checks the global policy settings.

linkedPullRequests.title: ifupdown2: Don't check for new IP addresses if dhcp-wait is set to no
linkedPullRequests.author: saiarcot895
linkedPullRequests.body:
Add a patch in ifupdown2 such that if DHCP is used for an interface, and
the policy setting sets dhcp-wait to no (meaning don't wait for dhclient
to acquire an IP address), then don't check to see if the interface has
a new IP address, since dhclient will still be working.

Fixes #8512.

Signed-off-by: Saikrishna Arcot <sarcot@microsoft.com>

#### Why I did it

SONiC ZTP (zero-touch provisioning) needs `dhcp-wait` to be set to `no` for ifupdown2, so that it won't wait for dhclient to get an address before moving on to the next interface. Since setting that policy then causes a failure (because of checks that ifupdown2 does to see if dhclient succeeded), add a patch to have it not check and see if dhclient succeeded or not.

#### How I did it

#### How to verify it

Within a KVM image:
1. Log into console.
2. Bring down eth0 using `sudo ifdown eth0`.
3. Edit `/etc/network/interfaces` so that `eth0` gets an address via dhcp, instead of being statically configured. Remove all of the lines in that section for static configuration.
4. On the host machine, start a DHCP server (dhcpd, dnsmasq, or similar), and have it listen on the br1 interface.
5. In the console connection, run `sudo ifup eth0`.
6. Verify that `eth0` has an IP address.
